_purpose: The Product Backlog + Sprint Backlog (Scrum-inspired, adapted for AI-executed work -- see docs/interview-scenarios/ and the 2026-09-18 overnight design conversation for the full reasoning). Every non-trivial task Claude does gets an entry here, SIZED before work starts (Small/Medium/Large/XLarge -- the current official Scrum term is 'size', not 'estimate' -- Claude, the one doing the work, is responsible for sizing it, per the 2020 Scrum Guide's own principle). 'status' distinguishes Product Backlog (backlog) from Sprint Backlog (active) from done work. A 'sprint' here is NOT a fixed timebox -- it's the variable-length span of one sized item, start to finish (see design rationale below). This is a lean, unscheduled first version deliberately: no automated retro subagent yet -- prove size-vs-actual comparison works manually first, per the Owner's own 'don't build the waste-risk before proving the simple version' call.

_sizing_rubric.SMALL: One clear sub-ask, one file or a tightly-scoped handful, follows an existing pattern in this codebase, low ambiguity.
_sizing_rubric.MEDIUM: A few distinct sub-asks or files, may touch 2 layers (e.g. backend + frontend), mostly follows existing patterns with some new logic.
_sizing_rubric.LARGE: Multiple sub-asks/files/subsystems, meaningful new logic or design decisions, real ambiguity requiring investigation before implementation.
_sizing_rubric.XLARGE: Cross-cutting, genuinely novel (no existing pattern to extend), high ambiguity, likely spans multiple work sessions.

_design_rationale: Sized item = the natural 'sprint' unit, not a fixed clock, because there is exactly one executor working sequentially (no multi-person sync problem a fixed timebox exists to solve). Retro/correction is a SEPARATE, later phase -- deliberately not built yet, to avoid the exact waste this system exists to prevent (an elaborate measurement system costing more than it saves). This file alone, plus the sizing discipline, is Phase 1.

items.title: Kafka: ContractPlanEnrolled event with real fan-out to 2 independent consumers
items.description: Second real event type through the existing transactional-outbox/Kafka infrastructure (see docs/FLAGSHIP_MARKET_COVERAGE.md's Eventing row for the first). Generalized OutboxPublisher/KafkaMessagingConfig from one hardcoded topic to an eventType->topic registry. Fanned out to 2 independent consumer groups (Notification, BillingSync) -- Kafka delivers each group its own full copy of the topic. Found and fixed a real bug this exposed: ProcessedEvent's idempotency ledger was keyed by eventId alone, correct only when exactly one consumer processes a given event; moved to a composite (consumerName, eventId) key (V7 migration).
items.size_rationale: 17 files touched across event/messaging/outbox/service layers; genuinely new logic (topic-routing generalization, composite-key idempotency redesign), not just pattern-following; real ambiguity required investigation (how to scope idempotency correctly, whether to generalize DLT routing too) before implementation -- not MEDIUM. Sized in retrospect (see LESSONS.md's sizing-discipline entry) after the fact but using the same rubric as if sized up front.

items.title: Redis: distributed lock for contract-plan enrollment concurrency
items.description: Layered defense-in-depth over the existing uq_contract_plan_one_active_per_customer DB constraint: a short-TTL Redis lock (SETNX + Lua-script token-owned release, avoiding the classic 'delete someone else's lock after my TTL expired' bug) acquired before ContractPlanService.enroll()'s critical section, released only after the transaction commits (TransactionSynchronizationManager.afterCompletion, not a plain finally -- releasing earlier would reopen the exact race the lock exists to close). A losing request gets a clean 409 (EnrollmentInProgressException) instead of racing to the database and surfacing a raw 500. Graceful fallback when Redis is unreachable: proceed without app-level locking, relying solely on the DB constraint, same philosophy as ContractPlanCacheService.
items.size_rationale: New service (EnrollmentLockService) with a genuinely novel-to-this-codebase pattern (token-owned Lua-script release, transaction-synchronization-timed release), new exception + GlobalExceptionHandler mapping, 2 new test files including a real concurrent-threads integration test -- meaningful new design decisions, not pattern-following. Sized in retrospect, same caveat as BL-003.
